title: A queen odour mediates reproductive suppression in a eusocial mammal.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Pulled the full file listing of the Edmond (Max Planck data repository) dataset doi:10.17617/3.7QCU1F through its API: 241 files, 144 GB total, CC0 licence. It holds 201 raw GC-MS (gas chromatography-mass spectrometry) .CDF chromatograms totalling 5.3 GB, but only 103 distinct file sizes, so many look like copies under different names (e.g. Queen1.CDF, Queen_rep1.CDF and 26_F_ID029_..._rep1.CDF are all 24,106,376 bytes). The rest is light-sheet brain images of 1-9 GB each, a 19.5 GB fUSI (functional ultrasound imaging) zip, a phylogenetic tree and short R/MATLAB scripts. There is no csv, tsv or xlsx metadata table anywhere in the deposit.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The claim of 771 volatile-profile samples from 351 naked mole-rats, the group sizes (e.g. 52 non-breeders from 8 colonies, n=5-13 per group in most experiments), and the hormone and behaviour measurements. Source-data spreadsheets are said to come with the paper, but the Europe PMC supplementary-file request timed out after 75 s, so I didn't open them.

a1_downloadable.note: Checked: the Edmond deposit is public under CC0 with no files restricted. Behavioural videos are 'available on request' only.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Checked: there is no metadata table. Breeding status (queen, female, male) and animal ID appear only in inconsistent file names (Queen7.CDF, 3161_rep4.CDF, Baby3.CDF), so the label would have to be reconstructed from file names and the paper text.

a3_inputs_present.note: Checked: the inputs are raw netCDF chromatograms. Turning them into a feature table needs XCMS (a peak-picking tool) to be run on them, and no processed peak table is deposited.

a4_units_stated.note: The raw files hold uncalibrated peak intensities. Only isopropyl myristate (IPM) was calibrated to ng, according to the paper.

a5_enough_rows.note: Checked: 201 deposited chromatograms, but only 103 distinct by size, and replicates cluster under each animal. The paper reports 351 animals; queens number about 13 by file name. Both are far below the ~400-row floor for classification.

a6_fits_laptop.note: The GC-MS subset is borderline; the imaging data (over 100 GB) is out of scope.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: The paper says 771 samples; the deposit has 201 CDF files, about half of them apparent duplicates under different names. There is no manifest to reconcile the two.

a8_label_provenance.note: Breeding status is observed directly (queens are the animals that breed), not predicted by a model, per the paper.

backbone.name: none (raw GC-MS spectra have no standard open freeze-and-head backbone in the approved list)

controls.positive_control: The IPM peak separating queens from non-breeders (from the paper)
controls.external_validation: Fukomys mole-rat species profiles (Taragaryen/Tully files, n=5-6 per species)

honest_claim_h3: At best: separates queen from non-breeder odour profiles among about 13 queens in a few captive Berlin and South African colonies, where one known compound (IPM) already does the job.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use whole-body odour chemical profiles to predict whether a naked mole-rat is the breeding queen or a non-breeder.
plain_idea.train_on: Raw gas chromatography-mass spectrometry traces of each animal's odour: 201 deposited files, about 103 of them distinct, with no table linking files to animals.
plain_idea.predict: Breeding status (queen, non-breeding female or male), taken from colony observation and recoverable only from file names.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Of little use: a single compound (IPM) already separates queens almost perfectly, so a model adds nothing over a one-peak threshold.

ml_idea: Classify breeding status from GC-MS (gas chromatography-mass spectrometry) odour profiles. It fails on size, on the missing metadata, and because a single-peak threshold on IPM (isopropyl myristate) already solves it.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated, because the project failed Part A.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the distinct animals with known breeding status in the deposit: about 13 queens, no manifest, about half the files duplicated by size.

verdict_reason: Fails A2, A3, A5 and A7, all checked against the file listing. The deposit holds 201 raw GC-MS chromatograms (only about 103 distinct by size) with no metadata table, labels only in file names, and roughly 13 queens. The paper's 771 samples don't match the deposit, and a single compound already separates the classes, so the ML question isn't worth asking. C2 not audited (stopped at Part A).
